;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Ukraine International Airlines Flight 752]], [[2019–20 Iranian protests]]
**[[Iran]]'s [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]] admits it mistakenly shot down the [[Ukraine International Airlines]] plane as it took off from [[Tehran]], killing all 176 aboard. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/iran-unintentionally-shot-ukrainian-jetliner-68209842 (ABC News)]
**[[Vigil]]s in Iran that were held for the victims subsequently turn into protests. According to [[Twitter]] videos, hundreds of protesters in Tehran call for the resignation of Supreme Leader Ayatollah [[Ali Khamenei]]. [https://reuters.com/article/amp/idUSKBN1ZA0LZ (Reuters)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/01/iranian-protesters-demand-khamenei-quit-downing-plane-200111171757858.html (Al Jazeera)]
**The [[List of diplomats of the United Kingdom to Iran|British ambassador to Iran]], [[Robert Macaire (diplomat)|Robert Macaire]], is arrested during anti-[[Government of Iran|government]] protests, after attending a vigil and then, according to [[BBC]], getting his hair cut. According to [[Tasnim News Agency]] he was arrested "on suspicion of organising, provoking and directing radical actions". [[Secretary of State for Foreign and Commonwealth Affairs|U.K. Foreign Secretary]] [[Dominic Raab]] states the arrest is in "flagrant violation" of [[international law]]. More than an hour later, Macaire is released from custody. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/jan/11/british-ambassador-arrested-at-demonstration-in-tehran-reports (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Libyan peace process]]
**[[Chancellor of Germany|German Chancellor]] [[Angela Merkel]] announces she will hold peace talks in [[Berlin]] to help end the [[Libyan Civil War (2014–present)|Second Libyan Civil War]]. Both [[President of Russia|Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] and [[Government of National Accord]] leader [[Fayez al-Sarraj]] express support for the peace initiative. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-russia-germany-merkel-libya/german-chancellor-merkel-says-berlin-will-host-libya-peace-talks-idUSKBN1ZA0NG (Reuters)]
**Forces loyal to [[Khalifa Haftar]] say they accept a ceasefire starting on 12 January, conditional on their rivals' acceptance. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-libya-security/libyan-forces-loyal-to-haftar-announces-conditional-ceasefire-spokesman-idUSKBN1ZA0WM (Reuters)]
*[[Iraqi protests (2019–present)]]
**Hundreds walk the street in mourning after popular journalist Ahmad Abdessamad and his cameraman were killed by unidentified gunmen the night before. [https://www.france24.com/en/20200111-hundreds-mourn-reporters-shot-dead-after-covering-iraq-protests (France 24)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**Two [[United States Armed Forces|United States troops]] are killed and another two troops injured by a [[Improvised explosive device|roadside bomb]]. The [[Taliban]] later claim responsibility. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-blast/two-u-s-service-members-killed-in-afghanistan-nato-idUSKBN1ZA0KT (Reuters)] [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/2-american-troops-killed-by-roadside-bomb-in-afghanistan-2020-01-11/ (CBS News)]
*[[Battle of Chinagodrar]]
**The death toll from the attack on Niger's armed forces on Thursday rises to over 89 [[Niger Armed Forces|Niger soldiers]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/reuters/2020/01/11/world/africa/11reuters-niger-security.html (''The New York Times'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[Winter Storm Isaiah]] brings widespread heavy snowfall and freezing rain to the [[Midwestern United States|midwestern]] and [[southern United States]], killing at least 12 people. [https://www.abc12.com/content/news/Recovery-begins-after-storms-that-kill-12-in-Midwest-South-566924641.html (Associated Press)]

;International relations
*[[North Korea–United States relations]]
**After [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] sends birthday wishes to [[List of leaders of North Korea|North Korean leader]] [[Kim Jong-un]], North Korea state media says that "although Chairman Kim Jong-un has good personal feelings about President Trump, they are, in the true sense of the word, 'personal'", and that it is not enough to resume denuclearization talks. It further stated that the country would not be led on the basis of Kim's feelings. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-northkorea-usa/north-korea-says-leaders-relations-not-enough-after-trump-sends-birthday-wishes-to-kim-idUSKCN1ZA082 (Reuters)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-51074956 (BBC News)]
*[[United Kingdom–United States relations]], [[Death of Harry Dunn]]
**The [[United States Department of State|U.S. State Department]] rejects an [[extradition]] request from the [[Home Office]] for the [[unlawful killing]] of Harry Dunn, describing it as "highly inappropriate" and "establish[ing] an extraordinarily troubling precedent". [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-northamptonshire-51075235 (BBC News)]
*[[Saudi Arabia–United States relations]]
**More than a dozen [[Saudi Arabia|Saudi]] [[Armed Forces of Saudi Arabia|military]] cadets are to be expelled from the [[United States]], following a review by the [[United States Department of Defense|Department of Defense]] in the aftermath of [[Naval Air Station Pensacola shooting|a shooting]] at [[Naval Air Station Pensacola]] last month by a [[Royal Saudi Air Force]] member. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/01/11/politics/saudi-servicemen-expelled-december-air-force-base-shooting/index.html (CNN)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Taiwanese presidential election]], [[2020 Taiwanese legislative election]]
**[[Taiwan]]ese voters head to the polls to elect a [[President of the Republic of China|president]] and a new session to the [[Legislative Yuan]]. Incumbent [[Taiwan independence movement|pro-independence]] President [[Tsai Ing-wen]] defeats [[Chinese unification|anti-independence]] challenger [[Han Kuo-yu]] in a landslide victory by more than 20%. [https://www.scmp.com/news/china/politics/article/3045652/taiwan-votes-not-just-leader-way-forward-beijing (''South China Morning Post'')]
**The governing [[Democratic Progressive Party]] retains its majority in the Yuan, albeit with fewer seats. Most of the seats lost are taken by third parties instead of the KMT. [https://www.taiwannews.com.tw/en/news/3855186 (''Taiwan News'')]
*[[Oman]] names [[Haitham bin Tariq|Haitham bin Tariq al-Said]] as its new head of state after the death of [[Sultan of Oman|Sultan]] [[Qaboos bin Said|Qaboos]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/01/11/middleeast/oman-sultan-qaboos-bin-said-death-intl/index.html (CNN International)]
*[[Politics of Northern Ireland]], [[Executive of the 6th Northern Ireland Assembly]]
**Following a deal brokered by the [[Government of the United Kingdom|British]] and [[Government of Ireland|Irish]] governments, the [[Northern Ireland Executive]] is restored with [[Democratic Unionist Party]] leader [[Arlene Foster]] as [[First Minister and deputy First Minister of Northern Ireland|First Minister]] and [[Sinn Féin]] deputy leader [[Michelle O'Neill]] as [[First Minister and deputy First Minister of Northern Ireland|deputy First Minister]], ending three years of political deadlock. The [[Executive of the 5th Northern Ireland Assembly|previous government]] had collapsed in 2017 as the result of a [[Renewable Heat Incentive scandal|renewable energy scandal]] involving Foster. [https://www.euronews.com/2020/01/10/northern-ireland-parliament-at-stormont-to-return-after-three-years-of-deadlock (Euronews)]
*Thousands of protestors march in [[Warsaw]] against [[Polish judicial disciplinary panel law|a controversial law]] proposed by the [[Sejm]] that would allow the [[Poland|Polish]] government to discipline judges that question their reform policies. Critics say the law would undermine the independence of [[Judiciary of Poland|the judiciary]], and risks Poland's membership in the [[European Union]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-poland-judiciary-toga-march/thousands-protest-against-polands-plan-to-discipline-judges-idUSKBN1ZA0PD (Reuters)]
